In January 2012, I was sick of sitting on my book idea, so I put my butt in a chair and wrote. I messed around with characters, their motivations, interesting settings, and dialogue. Got up many mornings at 5 to write before work. At times it was disparaging and frustrating. Other times it was like visiting a different world and experiencing something like never before. With some perseverance I finished 3.5 years later.

I had never wrote a book before, so this whole process was new to me. One thing you should know about me is I don’t like to follow rules. I am pretty sure I broke, bent, and violated every rule in the writing rule-book (Amazon link). I wrote the book in first person from six different points of view. I edited every scene as I went. I have 8 characters total. If there was a rule I didn't break don't tell me about it because I might go back and change some things just to make sure. If you clicked the link above then you were as desperate as me at the beginning on finding help in someone else’s method to writing. I am sorry there is no writing rule-book. No one will give you the formula to writing a novel.

One thing that stood in my way through the whole process was my own views and ideas of what I wanted the book to be. Putting ideas on paper changed them. They became different than the pictures in my head. I told myself I would mimic Fahrenheit 451 and Brave New World, as my book is along the same vein. I questioned if I was setting myself up for failure with these ideal views, but in the end I never let myself get the best of me. So I kept at it. Showing myself that what I was trying to create is working and verifying it with a gut feeling. If there was no gut feeling then I reworked the scene till I had at least an inkling and moved on. There are a lot of scenes that I am not happy with but those will be reworked in the second draft to either get to that feeling or they will be taken out completely. That is all I have to go on as an artist.

If you are interested in what my book is about, here is an actual link to the first scene. (Actual Link). I hope you enjoy.

This is something I always thought was dumb about Reddit. It would be nice to post a link and still provide additional information instead of having to post a comment in your own thread like a filthy commoner. Instead of having to choose between a link or a discussion, there should only be one post type that includes both options.
Submitting a link should give the option of including a message with it.

Reddit may look dumb for not doing that, but it is a dumb idea.

The problem is that there is no good way to handle how it would be voted on. For example, someone posts a link to a good, informative article but has a controversial opinion for the self text. How would users vote on that?

Here's the kicker: that problem doesn't exist now because if the 'self text' (comment in this case) is stupid, the article will still have a positive score while the stupid comment is downvoted. Why create unnecessary problems for 'convenience'?

I know many of you already know about suboxone, but when I was deep into my opiate use I had never heard of it.

I'm glad I did find out because I've been using it for three years and it saved my life. I simply couldn't afford dope anymore, I couldn't sustain r hustle to keep a bit of money going. I was done with life and being dope sick everyday was pushing me to suicide.

When I started suboxone I wasn't happy about it, I wanted to keep using dope. But I quickly found out the suboxone freed me from my worst feeling of being dope sick. Now I could live life normally and I could still get high if I wanted to. But I decided that I didn't need to anymore. I quit dope, weed, cigarettes and alcohol. I'm much more healthy and don't ever worry about money. I'm only saying this because I hope someone reads it and thinks, wow I want that too.

Now suboxone is expensive. Most doctors charge cash for all visits. 100-300 per visit depending on the doctor. The prescription itself can cost between 200-500 depending on what the doctor gives you.

50 suboxone strips = $500 cash

50 generic suboxone tablets = $200 cash

I've heard that Bunavil is cheaper.

If you have insurance you might be able to pay a co-pay or at least pay cash until you reach your deductible then pay a copay. I have state Medicaid and don't pay anything, totally recommend it!

Suboxone doctors also drug test, some all the time and some hardly ever. Your first few visits will be tested for sure.

OK that's all I have to say for now, if anyone any questions please message me or whatever.

I've created a subverse for suboxone /v/suboxone if anyone wants to contribute.
Suboxone. A life saving alternative for opiate users.

I'm glad it helped you. Readers should be aware, however, that it isn't such a miracle drug for everyone. My body didn't seem to metabolize it well, for example, and to get adequate relief, I'd have to take 24-32mg, and even then, I'd still feel off and have cravings. So don't feel discouraged if you try suboxone and you aren't magically cured of your addiction!
